title: SAK-50813 Site titles with ampersands distorted during publishing
body:
Jira: https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-50813

This proposed fix is preliminary, showing one proposed solution (uncommented) and an alternative (commented out), acknowledging that there may be other approaches. 

The first proposed solution (uncommented) is very specific, narrowly focused on fixing the issue with ampersands, which is a common character to be found in site titles (at least for our institution). This approach might valid/good-enough as I cannot think of other HTML meta-characters that are allowable for the Site Title (in Site Info > Edit Site Information); for example, greater than or less than characters are filtered out (when directly entered as is) by the time a revision to the title is to be confirmed (again, via Site Info > Edit Site Information).  That said, the approach of this first proposed solution might have overlooked valid characters (which in turn might be resolved with additional StringUtils.replace statements, if there aren't many).  

The other approach using convertFormattedTextToPlaintext (commented out) will resolve also the ampersand issue. It may also care for other HTML metacharacters overlooked. This approach however might be deemed too broad. 

Once a consensus is reached among reviewers, I can revise this PR to implement the agreed upon approach prior to merging to trunk.

SAK-51153 Sitestats: Event collection duplicates event processing
body:
https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51153

We found this while testing. This is a real case:

---

**17:21:48.463** → Finished reading events **3137257703 to 3137268571**. A total of **10,868** events were read (`sqlBlockSize` is **10,000**) (**868 events have no session**).  

**17:23:56.049** → Finished processing events up to **3137268571**.  

**17:23:56.477** → Reads event ID **3137278134** for the first time. The event is at position **10,431**, exceeding the queue.  
**17:23:56.495** → Finished reading events **3137267703 to 3137278651**. A total of **10,948** events were read (**948 events have no session**).  
(The last event processed in the previous queue was **3137268571**, but now it starts at **3137267703**, repeating **868** events.)

**17:26:14.342** → Finished processing events up to **3137278651**.  

**17:26:14.361** → Reads event ID **3137278134** for the second time. The event is at position **431**.  
**17:26:14.750** → Finished reading events **3137277703 to 3137288542**. A total of **10,839** events were read (**839 events have no session**).  
(The last event processed in the previous queue was **3137278651**, but now it starts at **3137277703**, repeating **948** events.)

**17:28:23.217** → Finished processing events up to **3137288542**.

---

The issue is that the SQL query returns exactly `sqlBlockSize` rows, excluding events from invalid sessions. As a result, if `sqlBlockSize` is 1000 and the first `eventId` is 5000, and the query encounters 100 invalid sessions, it will return events from 5000 to 6100. However, the next batch starts collecting from 6000 (5000 + 1000), causing 100 events to be processed twice.

I've added an `if` statement that should never be reached, but it doesn't hurt to make sure.

Refactored the GbModalWindow component to address several focus management and accessibility issues:

- Replaced naive initial focus on the first input element. The modal now defaults to focusing the main content panel itself. Added `setInitialFocusComponent()` method to allow explicitly setting a specific component to receive initial focus.

This uses a namespaced event listener attached to the document to reliably capture key events.

- Removed the `positionAtTop` functionality and associated JavaScript, allowing the modal to use default browser/Wicket positioning logic.

title: SAK-49085 Assignments alter group locking
body:
I have not tested or reviewed.

----------------------------------

1. Modified the AssignmentServiceImpl to not lock groups immediately when an assignment is posted but instead check the open date:
    - If the open date is in the future, groups remain unlocked
    - If the open date has already passed, groups are locked immediately
  2. Created two scheduled jobs:
    - AssignmentGroupLockingJob: Runs periodically to check for assignments about to open and locks their groups
    - AssignmentGroupUnlockingJob: Handles cases where an assignment's open date has been pushed into the future after it was posted
  3. Added unit tests for both jobs to ensure proper locking/unlocking behavior under different scenarios
  4. Created comprehensive documentation explaining the new behavior

  This implementation allows instructors to create and post assignments in advance without immediately locking groups, giving them flexibility to adjust group membership until the assignment actually opens. The system will
  automatically lock groups when the open date arrives to maintain the integrity of group-based submissions.

  The code also handles special cases such as:
  - Assignments with submissions (keeping groups locked even if the open date changes)
  - Lessons access groups (using a different lock mode)

Space keys can be reported as " ", "Space", or the older "Spacebar" - and some code still relies on keyCode === 32. title: SAK-51565 Gradebook fix reordering in Categories
body:
What we changed:

1. Removed Wicket AJAX behavior - No more setupAccordionBehavior() calls that destroy/recreate DOM elements
2. Kept Bootstrap accordion attributes - The HTML already has proper data-bs-toggle="collapse" attributes
3. Added JavaScript state persistence - Uses localStorage instead of server-side state management
4. Set initial CSS classes only - Java just sets the right CSS classes based on this.expanded

Why this fixes the sortable issue:

- No DOM destruction - Bootstrap accordion only toggles CSS classes (show/hide) on existing elements
- jQuery UI sortable survives - Since the table DOM elements are never destroyed, the sortable behavior remains attached
- Pure client-side - No AJAX requests that could interfere with JavaScript behaviors

Benefits:
- Better performance - No server round-trips for accordion state
- Preserves all JavaScript behaviors - Sortable, event handlers, etc. stay intact
- Simpler code - Less Java logic, more standard Bootstrap
- State persistence - Accordion state saved across page reloads via localStorage

The drag-and-drop should now work perfectly because the DOM elements with ksortable attached are never destroyed by AJAX updates!

title: SAK-51608 Samigo exports should use the XLSX format
body:
1. Modern Standard

  - XLSX is the current standard - Excel has used XLSX as the default format since 2007 (18+ years ago)
  - XLS is legacy - The old binary format is from Excel 97-2003 and is increasingly unsupported
  - Future-proofing - Modern spreadsheet applications expect XLSX

  2. Better Compatibility

  - Cross-platform support - XLSX works better with LibreOffice, Google Sheets, Numbers, and other non-Microsoft tools
  - Mobile compatibility - Better support on tablets and phones
  - Cloud integration - Modern cloud services (Google Drive, OneDrive, etc.) handle XLSX better

  3. Technical Advantages

  - No artificial limits - The old code only used XLSX for 255+ columns, but XLSX is better for ANY number of columns
  - Better compression - XLSX files are typically smaller due to XML compression
  - Unicode support - Better handling of international characters and special symbols
  - Metadata support - XLSX supports richer document properties

  4. User Experience Improvements

  - Filename sanitization - Fixes the garbled character issue (&lt^^x3B^ → clean underscores)
  - Consistent behavior - No more "sometimes XLS, sometimes XLSX" confusion
  - Professional appearance - XLSX is what users expect in 2025

SAK-51639 Grader fix grade input not updating when navigating between students
body:
## The Root Cause

  The problem wasn't with Lit's rendering or the live() directive. The issue was with data management:

  1. When a user types in the grade input, the _gradeSelected method modifies the submission object directly in the _submissions array
  2. When navigating between students, the component was using the modified submission objects from _submissions
  3. The modified data persisted because the submissions array contained the user's typed values, not the original saved grades

## The Proper Fix

  Instead of trying to force DOM updates, I fixed the data flow by:

  1. Reverting unsaved changes when switching students, just like the Cancel button does
  2. Using originalSubmissions to restore the unmodified data
  3. Applying this logic to all navigation methods: _previous(), _next(), and _studentSelected()

  This ensures that unsaved grade changes are discarded when navigating away, which is the correct UX behavior - users should save their changes or lose them when navigating.

Fixes percentage grades appearing blank (-) in student grade summary after

calculateEquivalentPercent() to getPercentEarned() for percentage gradebooks.

Restored original percentage calculation logic in convertGradeRecordToGradeDefinition()
to properly calculate percentage from pointsEarned/pointsPossible while maintaining
the performance benefits of the bulk grade fetching optimization.

  - But GradeSummaryTablePanel was looking for "gradeType"
  - This caused gradeType to always be null
  - Result: Percentage logic NEVER triggered, always used points display

## The Fix:
```java
  // BEFORE (broken):
  tableModel.put("gradingType", gradebook.getGradeType());

  // AFTER (fixed):
  tableModel.put("gradeType", gradebook.getGradeType());
```

title: SAK-51736 Content: Default to UTF-8 charset for text-based files served via direct access
body:
This commit fixes a long-standing issue where text-based files (CSS, Python, JavaScript, etc.) containing non-ASCII characters display garbled when accessed directly through Sakai's access servlet. Characters like "ñ", "á", and "é" were appearing as "Ã±", "Ã¡", and "Ã©" respectively.

The root cause is that browsers in 2025 still don't default to UTF-8 encoding when no charset is specified in the HTTP Content-Type header. Instead, they fall back to:
- Platform-specific defaults (Windows-1252 on Windows, ISO-8859-1 on Linux)
- Heuristic detection (unreliable and inconsistent)
- System locale settings

This creates a vicious cycle where legacy web content prevents browsers from defaulting to UTF-8, even though UTF-8 has been the de facto standard for new content for over a decade.

SOLUTION:
Modified BaseContentService.java to explicitly set "charset=UTF-8" for all text/* content types when no explicit encoding property exists. This approach:

1. Only affects text-based files (leaves binary files untouched)
2. Preserves existing behavior for files with explicit encoding properties
3. Provides a sensible UTF-8 default for user-uploaded text files
4. Fixes the display issue without breaking existing functionality

This is a minimal, targeted fix compared to the complex response wrapper approach in the original PR. UTF-8 is the only sane assumption for text content in 2025 - it's backwards-compatible with ASCII and supports all Unicode characters.

title: SAK-51894 Lessons imported, unvisited pages are listed as not in use
body:
Untested fix from Codex, ChatGPT 5 thinking=high

### What I changed

- Proactively create top-level SimplePageItems for any top-level Lessons pages missing them.
- Runs before building the Index list, so traversal includes these pages and removes them from the “unused” bucket.
- After creating vestigial pages for missing placements, iterate all site pages:
  - For each top-level Lessons page (parent == null, has a valid `toolId`, not a student page), if no top-level SimplePageItem exists, create it via `makeItem(... PAGE, sakaiId=pageId, title)` and `quickSaveItem`.

### Why this addresses the bug

Index of Pages builds reachability from top-level items; if an imported top-level page exists but its corresponding top-level item was not created by import yet, that page (and its subpages) are considered “unused”. By eagerly creating the missing items, the index’s traversal includes these pages immediately after import, regardless of whether they’ve been visited.

title: SAK-51889 Lessons draft announcements showing in embedded widget
body:
This commit fixes two related bugs in the Lessons embedded announcements component:

1. **Draft announcements visible to instructors**: Draft announcements were showing in the Lessons embedded widget without draft labels, confusing instructors who might think the announcements were published.

2. **NullPointerException in announcement sorting**: A NPE was occurring when sorting announcements due to null originChannel values.

## Root Cause Analysis

The issues stem from SAK-49604 (ca2134e1831) which simplified channel handling in the announcement sorting logic but introduced a regression:

**Before SAK-49604:**
- Each message had its originChannel properly set from its actual channel
- Draft filtering worked correctly

**After SAK-49604:**
- All messages used defaultChannel, leaving originChannel = null
- NPE occurred in AnnouncementWrapper constructor when calling getOriginChannel().equals()
- NPE masked the fact that ViewableFilter wasn't filtering drafts properly for instructors

## The Fixes

### Fix 1: Explicit Draft Filtering (AnnouncementEntityProviderImpl.java)
- Added explicit draft checks in both main and fallback code paths
- Main path: Filter drafts after ViewableFilter since instructors can normally see their own drafts
- Fallback path: Added missing draft check that was only in main path

### Fix 2: Null Safety (AnnouncementWrapper.java)
- Added null check for originChannel before calling .equals()
- Prevents NPE when originChannel is not set (common for non-merged announcements)

## Impact
- Draft announcements no longer appear in Lessons embedded widget
- NPE in announcement sorting is prevented
- Instructors won't see confusing draft announcements in Lessons
- Normal Announcement tool functionality unchanged

title: SAK-51763 Content improve deduplicate logic for identical uploads
body:
## Problem Summary
Single-instance store had a critical bug where "Upload New Version"
or "Edit Content" operations could cause content to leak between different sites when
files previously shared the same SHA256 hash.

### Root Cause
The `putResourceBodyFilesystem()` method in `DbContentService.java` was:
1. Using the EXISTING file path from `m_filePath`
2. Overwriting that file with new content
3. THEN checking for duplicates (too late!)

This caused shared files to be overwritten, making new content visible to all sites
sharing that file path.

## Scenario That Caused Leakage
1. Site A uploads "file.txt" with content "Hello" → SHA256=abc123, FILE_PATH=/content/abc123.bin
2. Site B uploads "file.txt" with content "Hello" → SHA256=abc123, FILE_PATH=/content/abc123.bin (reused)
3. Site A does "Upload New Version" with content "Goodbye"
   - Overwrites /content/abc123.bin with "Goodbye"
   - Both sites now see "Goodbye"! 🚨

## Fix Implementation

### 1. Fixed `putResourceBodyFilesystem()` (kernel level)
**Before:** Save file → Calculate SHA256 → Check duplicates (too late!)
**After:** Calculate SHA256 → Check duplicates → Decide path → Save file

Key changes:
- Buffer content to calculate SHA256 BEFORE saving
- Check for duplicates BEFORE writing any files
- Smart path decision:
  - New unique content → Generate new UUID path
  - Duplicate content → Reuse existing path (single-instance store works!)
  - Replacement with same hash → Force new path (prevent self-overwrite)
- Proper cleanup of old files with reference counting

### 2. Fixed `replaceContent()` and `reviseContent()` in ResourcesAction
- Both methods now use `editResource()` which properly triggers the fixed kernel code
- Preserves original filenames (no more file.txt → file-1.txt)
- Maintains proper content isolation between sites

## Technical Details

### Database Changes
- FILE_PATH field now properly updates during content replacement
- SHA256 field correctly reflects new content
- No schema changes required

### Single-Instance Store Behavior
- ✅ Still works for new uploads (deduplication preserved)
- ✅ Still works when multiple sites upload identical content
- ✅ Fixed: No longer shares file paths during replacement operations
- ✅ Fixed: FILE_PATH properly updates when content changes

### Safety Mechanisms
- Reference counting before file deletion
- Transactional safety during updates
- Proper error handling for I/O operations

## Testing Recommendations
1. Upload same file to multiple sites
2. Use "Upload New Version" with different content
3. Verify each site maintains correct content
4. Check that single-instance store still deduplicates new uploads
5. Monitor disk usage to ensure proper cleanup

## Performance Impact
Minimal - The fix adds:
- One buffer operation (readAllBytes) for SHA256 calculation
- One database query for duplicate checking (already existed, just moved earlier)
- Negligible memory usage for buffering

title: SAK-51920 Assignments preserve anonymous grading checkbox after past-due alert
body:
**Problem**: When an instructor edits an assignment after its due date, the form shows an alert about the due date being in the past. After the alert, the form re-renders and the checkbox for anonymous grading is unexpectedly cleared, forcing the instructor to re-check it before saving.

**Root cause**: In setAssignmentFormContext(...), the value used for  was always taken from the persisted assignment (assignmentService.assignmentUsesAnonymousGrading(a)) when editing an existing assignment. This overwrote the user’s in-progress selection captured in SessionState (NEW_ASSIGNMENT_CHECK_ANONYMOUS_GRADING) after validation, such as the past-due alert. As a result, the checkbox state did not persist across the validation round-trip.

**Fix**: Prefer the user’s in-progress selection from SessionState when it exists; otherwise fall back to the persisted value (or default when creating). Specifically: compute anonFromState = (Boolean) state.getAttribute(NEW_ASSIGNMENT_CHECK_ANONYMOUS_GRADING) and set anonGrading = anonFromState != null ? anonFromState : assignmentService.assignmentUsesAnonymousGrading(a) when editing; for new assignments, use anonFromState. The rest of the context remains unchanged.

**Why this is correct**: The checkbox posts to NEW_ASSIGNMENT_CHECK_ANONYMOUS_GRADING and we already store that into SessionState in setNewAssignmentParameters(...). When the form re-renders due to validation (e.g., past-due), the UI should reflect the user’s latest choice, not the previously persisted assignment value. This mirrors how other form fields are preserved via state on validation errors.

**Files changed**: assignment/tool/src/java/org/sakaiproject/assignment/tool/AssignmentAction.java — revised anonGrading computation inside setAssignmentFormContext(...) to use state-first fallback-to-persisted logic.

**Scope and risk**: Localized to context-value selection for the anonymous grading checkbox in the instructor new/edit assignment view. No changes to templates or services. Default behavior on first load is unchanged (still shows the persisted value when there’s no in-progress state). Low risk: purely affects in-form state retention during validation.

**Manual test plan**:

1) Edit an assignment whose due date is in the past. Check ‘Hide submitters’ identities…’. Click Post. Observe the alert about due date in the past. Scroll back down and verify the checkbox remains checked. Click Post again to save.

2) Edit an assignment whose due date is in the future (no alert). Toggle anonymous grading and Post—value should save as expected.

3) Create a new assignment and trigger a different validation error (e.g., inconsistent open/close times). Ensure the checkbox state persists after the page re-renders.

4) Re-open the edit form to confirm the persisted value is reflected on initial load (no in-progress state).

Notes: Velocity templates already bind to ; no template updates required. Verified other contexts read-only consume this value and are unaffected (grading lists, submissions, preview).

title: SAK-51839 Assignments legacy grader hide ability for Grade Overrides when anonymous group grading is selected
body:
**Problem**: In the Legacy grading interface, enabling "Assign Grade Overrides" for a group-submitted assignment with anonymous grading reveals student identities alongside per-user override inputs. This breaks anonymity. In the list view, per-user override markers could also be populated from context.

**Root cause**: The legacy grading template always rendered the Grade Overrides UI for group assignments with no check for anonymous grading. The server context and form handlers populated and processed per-user override values regardless of anonymity, so identities were displayed (labels) and overrides could be posted even when anonymized grading was enabled.

**Fix** (UI): In chef_assignments_instructor_grading_submission.vm, conditionally render the Grade Overrides toggle/panel only when the assignment is a group assignment and anonymous grading is NOT enabled (.IsGroup && !).

**Fix** (Server): In AssignmentAction, gate all Grade Overrides population/processing behind an anonymous grading check: (1) build_instructor_grade_submission_context: don’t set value_grades when anonymous; (2) build_instructor_grade_assignment_context (list view): don’t populate value_grades when anonymous; (3) putSubmissionInfoIntoState: don’t load existing per-user overrides when anonymous; (4) readGradeForm: ignore any per-user override inputs in anonymous mode. This prevents crafted POSTs from bypassing the UI and avoids leaking identity through override contexts.

**Behavior**: For anonymous group assignments, the Legacy grading UI no longer shows "Assign Grade Overrides" and server-side ignores override inputs. body:
- Taught the Unicode helpers about real code points. FormattedTextImpl.encodeUnicode now walks strings by Unicode code point instead of 16‑bit chars, so it turns 🙂 into 🙂 instead of the two bogus entities (��) that were blowing up the XML parser. Its inverse, decodeNumericCharacterReferences, got the same treatment so it can rebuild supplementary characters cleanly.
  - Made the announcement service use those helpers. When an announcement header is serialized, we now run the subject through formattedText.encodeUnicode before we drop it into the XML attribute. When we read a header back, we run decodeNumericCharacterReferences so the UI still sees the literal emoji. That guarantees any new announcement gets stored with a single valid numeric entity.
  - Stopped Xerces from shouting into stderr. StorageUtils.readDocumentFromString installs a custom SAX error handler, so if some old row still has a bad surrogate sequence we catch it, log the failure through SLF4J with a snippet that names the offending announcement, and carry on without the raw [Fatal Error] spam.
  - Unit tests and logging polish. I added regression cases that cover single and consecutive emoji in both encode/decode paths, and the new logger now tells you exactly which message is still dirty.

title: SAK-51968 Rubrics sync fix
body:
When an assignment uses a rubric and creates a gradebook item, users can edit the rubric association independently in both tools (Assignments and Gradebook). This results in two different rubric associations for the same item, which is confusing to instructors.

The issue occurs because:
1. Assignment tool stores rubric associations using tool ID `AssignmentConstants.TOOL_ID` (e.g., "sakai.assignment.grades")
2. Gradebook tool stores rubric associations using tool ID `RubricsConstants.RBCS_TOOL_GRADEBOOKNG` (e.g., "sakai.gradebookng")
3. Both use the same item ID but different tool IDs, creating separate records in `rbc_tool_item_rbc_assoc` table
4. Updates in one tool don't sync to the other tool's rubric association

Added bidirectional synchronization between assignment and gradebook rubric associations:

**File:** `gradebookng/tool/src/java/org/sakaiproject/gradebookng/tool/panels/AddOrEditGradeItemPanel.java`

- Added `syncRubricWithAssignment()` method that:
  - Checks if the gradebook item is externally maintained by assignment tool
  - If so, syncs the rubric association to the assignment tool using the external assignment ID
  - Only syncs when `externalAppName` equals `AssignmentConstants.TOOL_ID`

**File:** `assignment/tool/src/java/org/sakaiproject/assignment/tool/AssignmentAction.java`

- Added `syncRubricWithGradebook()` method that:
  - Checks if the assignment is associated with a gradebook item
  - If so, syncs the rubric association to the gradebook tool using the gradebook item ID
  - Uses the `PROP_ASSIGNMENT_ASSOCIATE_GRADEBOOK_ASSIGNMENT` property to find linked gradebook items

Both sync methods include robust error handling:
- Exceptions are caught and logged as warnings
- Sync failures don't break the primary operation (saving assignment/gradebook item)
- Detailed logging for troubleshooting

1. `gradebookng/tool/src/java/org/sakaiproject/gradebookng/tool/panels/AddOrEditGradeItemPanel.java`
   - Added imports for Assignment APIs and logging
   - Added `[user]` annotation for logging
   - Added `syncRubricWithAssignment()` method
   - Modified rubric save logic to call sync method

2. `assignment/tool/src/java/org/sakaiproject/assignment/tool/AssignmentAction.java`
   - Added `syncRubricWithGradebook()` method
   - Modified rubric save logic to call sync method

To verify the fix works correctly:

1. As an instructor, go to Rubrics and create 2+ rubrics (e.g., "Rubric A" and "Rubric B")
2. Go to Assignments and create an assignment with "Rubric A"
3. Select "Create new Gradebook item" to create a gradebook item
4. **Before fix:** Go to Gradebook → Edit Item Details → change rubric to "Rubric B" → Save

title: SAK-51953 site-manage add copy permission controls to site import
body:
Jira: https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51953

I made the following additional considerations with this attempt to meet the [design specification in Wilma’s comment in the corresponding jira](https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-51953?focusedCommentId=227926).


1. **Copying permissions overall:** I revised the logic for SiteManageServiceImpl.copyToolPermissions so that only permissions for tools selected by the instructor are copied. The logic introduced in July 2025 always copies permissions regardless of which tools are selected; however, it did so in a way which omitted the transferring of permissions if they were revoked in the ‘fromSite’.
2. **Copying permissions for the ‘replace’ option:** I only automatically set the ‘Copy permission’ option for tools an instructor initially selects. Otherwise, the instructor may need to deselect ‘Copy permissions’ for several tools they aren’t interested in importing.
3. **Gradebook & permissions:** I purposefully omitted a “Copy permissions” option for Gradebook because those permission settings, which are based on users, are not analogous to the permissions settings for other tools where importing makes sense.
4. **Resources & permissions:** I purposefully omitted a “Copy permissions” option for Resources because the copying permissions for Resources is not working currently, an issue that’s likely tied up with other jiras pertaining to Resources and permissions, and thus outside the intended scope of this jira. For now, omitting the “Copy permissions” option for Resources will not mislead instructors into thinking that these permissions will actually copy.
5. **Checkbox behavior (Part 1):** Whether or not permissions for a given tool and site are imported should be transparent to the user. Therefore, I’ve altered the display logic for the “options” link and the content it expands to be displayed by default. Options checkboxes can still be hidden by clicking the corresponding ‘options’ link.
6. **Checkbox behavior (Part 2):** The tool checkbox should serve as a “select all / deselect all” control for any tool item (entities) it may have.
7. **Gradebook entities:** I have removed any Gradebook entities that are externally managed (e.g., from Assignments, Tests & Quizzes, etc.) from being listed in Import from Site. Such items cannot be imported, nor should they, as such gradebook items are dependent on the tool from which they originate.

title: SAK-51890 Lessons fix import links to assignments
body:
The regression boiled down to AssignmentEntity.findObject(...) not being able to look up the new assignment that Lessons had just copied into the destination site.

  - Location: lessonbuilder/tool/src/java/org/sakaiproject/lessonbuildertool/service/AssignmentEntity.java:512 (the method that maps the old assignment reference to the newly created one).
  - What we saw: the transversalMap handed to Lessons during transferCopyEntities now contains entries like "/assignment/NEW_ID" -> "/assignment/OLD_ID". The existing code only ever called objectMap.get("assignment/OLD_ID"), so it never matched keys that started with / or entries where the new ID was on the value side.
  - Result: newassignment stayed null, Lessons fell through to the title-search fallback, and because the assignment was still draft (not yet published per the test plan) the fallback couldn’t see it. The SimplePage item kept pointing to /assignment/a/Site1/..., so the student link still targeted the original site.

The fix adds the missing lookups (accept the leading slash and scan for entries whose value equals the legacy id) so we recover /assignment/NEW_ID and update the Lessons item correctly.

title: SAK-51994 Scorm align ADLDuration units milliseconds vs seconds

The commit now converts schema-formatted durations to milliseconds in ADLDuration, but the Hibernate mapping still reads existing SCORM_ADL_DURATION_T.DURATION values without any migration. title: SAK-52163 Fix flaky tests across multiple modules
body:
### Summary
Fixes nondeterministic (flaky) test in following modules:
- rwiki/rwiki-impl/impl
- lti/tsugi-util
- lti/lti-common
- samigo/samigo-services

The failure was found with [NonDex](https://github.com/[user]/NonDex), which explores non-determinism in tests. These tests can cause test failure under different JVMs, etc.

### Notes
My ICLA (submitted and emailed on Nov 9) have not been approved and I do not have JIRA permission now either, therefore the branch name and commit message does not contain the right JIRA reference number. I submitted this PR considering it might be better to have maintainers review the fix as soon as possible. This commit only modifies testing code, but not any implementation code under test.

Please let me know if any changes are needed for this PR or if I should take additional steps to obtain JIRA permissions.

### Root Cause and Fix
- rwiki/rwiki-impl/impl
  - Cause: Inside `RWikiCurrentObjectImpl`, the fields in hashset `hs` could be iterated in differnt orders (`longString` may not be the first one iterated).
  - Fix: Replaced HashSet with LinkedHashSet in tests to ensure deterministic order when iterating over test inputs.
- lti/tsugi-util
  - Cause: 
The order of fields when using jackson Mapper is not guaranteed, as the
[jackson doc](https://fasterxml.github.io/jackson-databind/javadoc/2.7/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/MapperFeature.html) describes:
    > SORT_PROPERTIES_ALPHABETICALLY
    > Feature that defines default property serialization order used for POJO fields (note: does not apply to Map serialization!): if enabled, default ordering is alphabetic (similar to how JsonPropertyOrder.alphabetic() works); if disabled, order is unspecified (based on what JDK gives us, which may be declaration order, but is not guaranteed).
  - Fix: Changed JSON string equality checks to compare parsed `JsonNode` objects instead of raw strings, making tests independent of field order.

- lti/lti-common
  - Cause: The [JSONObject](https://github.com/[user]/JSON-java/blob/master/src/main/java/org/json/JSONObject.java) used here is internally unordered, causing the non-determinism:
    ```
    getKeySetJSON(Map<String, RSAPublicKey> keys) {
        ...
        JSONObject keyset = new JSONObject();
        keyset.put("keys", jar);

        String keySetJSON = keyset.toString();
        ...
    }
    ```
   - Fix: Check any field after parsing the JSON into JSON objects.
- samigo/samigo-services
  - Cause: Methods like preparePublishedItemCancellation() and preparePublishedItemHash() build unordered hashmap. Thus, when the items are re-collected into a new map, the logical order of them is lost.
  - Fix: Sort the items using itemIDs
    ```
    // Ensure deterministic order before comparing
    Comparator<ItemDataIfc> byId = Comparator.comparing(ItemDataIfc::getItemId);
    Arrays.sort(savedItems, byId);
    Arrays.sort(cancelledTestItems, byId);
    ```

### Failure Reproduction

1. Checkout the master branch and the recent commit I tested on: 0ccc34260bf2f5dd74054a05db471aebf89f044e
2. Build with Java 17 and  maven: 
> Apache Maven 3.9.11
3. Run test with [NonDex](https://github.com/[user]/NonDex), for example:
```
mvn edu.illinois:nondex-maven-plugin:2.1.7:nondex -pl rwiki/rwiki-impl/impl \
    -Dtest=uk.ac.cam.caret.sakai.rwiki.component.service.impl.test.RWikiObjectServiceImplTest#testExtractReferencesExtractReferencesTooLong \
    -Djacoco.skip -Drat.skip -Dpmd.skip -Denforcer.skip
```
4. Observe the test failure, for example:
```
[ERROR] Failures: 
[ERROR]   StatisticsServiceTest.testExtendedMatchingItem:520 expected:<1> but was:<0>
[INFO] 
[ERROR] Tests run: 1, Failures: 1, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
```

* **Tests**
  * Key-set tests now validate JSON structure and required fields (including kty) rather than relying on substring checks.
  * JSON log comparisons now assert structural equivalence by parsing and comparing JSON trees instead of exact string formatting.
  * Tests made deterministic by preserving insertion order and sorting item lists before comparison to ensure consistent results.

title: SAK-52333 portal Remove PortalRenderTest and supporting files
body:
https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52333

This commit removes the PortalRenderTest and MockCharonPortal because the latter was using an old and defunct version of JTidy and had to include workarounds for the lack of HTML5 awareness in the library. There is a new version of JTidy available which this commit upgrades portal to, however the PortalRenderTest was dumping errors into the output files which were effectively useless as they were based on the fully rendered outputs of our composed Velocity templates. Telling us that a quote is missing on line 311 of a 20 line template is not much use. Another issue is that JTidy doesn't recognise svg path tags or html fragments in single comma attributes.

My opinion is that we should be using a mixture of static analysis of the velocity template together with our current Cypress tests.

title: SAK-52382 Samigo fix ShowMedia download behavior for file-upload grading
body:
I made ShowMedia treat download behavior and MIME behavior as first-class, using kernel/CHS MIME as truth and preserving attachment headers in the grading flow.

  What was wrong before:

  1. Grading file links were inconsistent about forcing download.
  2. ShowMedia could rely on stale/generic MediaData.mimeType (application/octet-stream).
  3. Forced-download paths could lose filename semantics in optimized delivery paths.
  4. Browser then fell back to URL-based names like ShowMedia.

  What changed:

  1. Grading links now explicitly request forced download (setMimeType=false) in:

  - samigo/samigo-app/src/webapp/jsf/evaluation/item/displayFileUpload.jsp
  - samigo/samigo-app/src/webapp/jsf/evaluation/item/displayFileUploadAnswer.jsp

  2. ShowMediaServlet now:

  - Computes type from ContentResource.getContentType() first (kernel-detected), fallback to MediaData.mimeType.
  - Forces attachment for unknown/generic types or when setMimeType=false.
  - Avoids sending a misleading generic Content-Type header when type is unknown.
  - Always sets Content-Disposition for proper filename behavior.
  - Keeps noisy request logs at debug with useful structured content.

  3. On save, Samigo now syncs MediaData.mimeType from CHS after commit/update in:

  - samigo/samigo-services/src/java/org/sakaiproject/tool/assessment/facade/AssessmentGradingFacadeQueries.java

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved media file handling to ensure correct content type detection and consistent file download behavior.
  * Enhanced file upload display reliability with better metadata synchronization.
  * Refined media serving logic to correctly determine whether files should be displayed inline or downloaded as attachments.

title: SAK-52310 Samigo batch student list lookups
body: For [user]: I seeded a site with 200 open Samigo assessments, logged in as a real student, and traced the exact student Tests page request with Glowroot on Tomcat. That turned out to be much more useful than looking at MySQL slow queries, because the problem was not one giant SQL statement. It was a large number of smaller Hibernate-driven queries happening during a single page render. The first hotspot was `ExtendedTimeDeliveryService`. On the student list, Samigo was creating that service once per visible assessment. Each pass was re-fetching site and assessment data, plus extended-time data, which created a classic N+1 pattern. I changed that path to batch extended-time resolution for the whole visible list and removed the per-assessment `getPublishedAssessmentSiteId()` calls. On the page we were measuring, that dropped JDBC query count from 2457 to 852 and improved response time from about 2.0s to 1.6s. The second hotspot was secure delivery decoration in `SelectActionListener`. After the list was already built, Samigo was still calling `getPublishedAssessmentQuick()` once per assessment just to discover secure-delivery metadata. That call was not actually quick. It was pulling in full published assessment state, metadata, attachments, and secured IP data for every row. I replaced that with one batch metadata lookup for all visible assessments, and only ask the secure-delivery service for an alternate URL when a module id is actually present. After both fixes, the same student Tests page was down to about 1.3 seconds in Glowroot, with 225 JDBC queries total. At that point, the Samigo-specific query fan-out was essentially gone. The remaining hot SQL was mostly repeated `SAKAI_REALM` lookups coming from portal and site navigation permission checks, not from the assessment list itself. So the main improvement here is that the Samigo student list no longer does per-assessment extended-time and secure-delivery lookups. We now fetch that data in bulk, which makes the page much cheaper to render under a large assessment count. Glowroot was the tool that made this obvious because it let us look at one real request, count the SQL, and see exactly where the fan-out was happening. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Environment variable/system property support to override test passwords. * New batch APIs for extended-time and assessment metadata retrieval. * **Refactor** * Cleaner initialization flow for permissions to remove side effects. * Centralized extended-time resolution and application to reduce per-item work. * **Tests** * Added unit tests for secure delivery and extended-time logic. * Strengthened end-to-end tests with robust interaction helpers and timeouts. * **Performance Improvements** * Reduced per-item lookups via batched queries and precomputed maps. ### Before ### After

title: SAK-52430 Assignments resynchronize submitters when group submissions move
body:
Group assignment submissions persist two ownership signals: `ASN_SUBMISSION.GROUP_ID` and the submitter rows in `ASN_SUBMISSION_SUBMITTER`. The edit flow in `AssignmentAction` allowed an existing submission to be reassigned to a different group by updating only `groupId`. The persisted submitter roster was left untouched, which lets the submission drift into a split-brain state where grading resolves it under one group while student-facing views and grade posting still follow the stale submitter roster.

Tighten the reassignment path so the tool stops treating group changes as a plain setGroupId operation. When an existing group submission is moved to another assignment group, delegate to `AssignmentService.reassignGroupSubmission()`. That service method now validates the target `group`, enforces update-or-grade permission, rebuilds the stored submitter set from the target group's current eligible members, and guarantees that the reassigned submission still has a submittee by preferring the current editor, then the prior submittee, then the first eligible member. For overlapping members, reuse the existing submitter rows so per-submitter state is preserved where it still applies. The tool path now also aborts immediately if the destination group already has a submission instead of warning and then mutating `groupId` anyway.

Also add focused regression coverage for the service layer: one test verifies that changing groups replaces the submitter roster and persists the new group id, one verifies that a valid submittee is preserved even when the current editor is not in the destination group, and one verifies that the new reassignment entry point fails closed without submission update permission.

title: WIP sakai-table Add reusable data table web component
body:
## Summary

- **New `<sakai-table>` Lit web component** (`packages/sakai-table/`) — a single reusable data table registered globally on every Sakai page via `bundle-entry-points/base.js`
- **Migrated `ConversationsStatistics`** to use `<sakai-table>`, removing 200+ lines of hand-rolled sort/pager/table markup

## sakai-table features

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Two data modes** | `data` (client-side array) or `url` (server-side fetch with `?page&pageSize&sortField&sortOrder&search`) |
| **Columns config** | `[{ label, field, sortable?, hidden? }]` |
| **Sorting** | Accessible `<button>` headers with `aria-sort`, `sakai-icon` indicators, emits `sakai-table-sort` |
| **Pagination** | `<sakai-pager>` integration, emits `sakai-table-page` |
| **Search** | Optional text input, emits `sakai-table-search` |
| **Row selection** | Optional checkboxes + select-all, emits `sakai-table-selection-changed` |
| **Slots** | `toolbar` (group dropdowns, filters) and `actions` (per-row actions) |
| **i18n** | `sakai-table.properties` bundle |
| **Styling** | `class="table table-hover table-striped table-bordered"` — identical to existing Sakai tables |

## Usage

```html
<!-- Client-side -->
<sakai-table id="t" searchable selectable page-size="20"></sakai-table>
<script>
  const t = document.getElementById("t");
  t.columns = [{ label: "Title", field: "title", sortable: true }];
  t.data = [ /* server-rendered JSON */ ];
</script>

<!-- Server-side (endpoint returns { data: [], total: N }) -->
<sakai-table url="/api/my-tool/list" page-size="20" searchable></sakai-table>
```

## Research background

Sakai has ~104 data tables across 200+ files with 4 different sort mechanisms, 4 different pagination mechanisms, and 3 third-party table libraries. Of those, ~91 share the same Bootstrap table structure and are candidates for `<sakai-table>`. This PR establishes the component and proves the pattern with ConversationsStatistics. Subsequent PRs will migrate tools one at a time, each also adding the REST endpoint needed for server-side mode.

## Test plan

- [ ] Navigate to Conversations → Statistics in a site with activity
- [ ] Verify table renders with all 9 columns
- [ ] Click column headers — verify sort order flips and data re-fetches
- [ ] Change timeframe radio (This Week / All Time) — verify data re-fetches
- [ ] Verify pagination appears when results exceed page size
- [ ] Verify `<sakai-table>` element appears on non-Conversations pages (registered globally)

title: SAK-52040 Hierarchy migrate from genericdao to JPA
body:
Schema & Persistence Model
  - Replaced 4 separator-encoded string fields (DIRECTPARENTIDS, PARENTIDS, DIRECTCHILDIDS, CHILDIDS) on the old HierarchyPersistentNode entity with a self-referential [user] JPA relationship backed by a new HIERARCHY_NODE_PARENTS join table
  - Added DDL migration scripts for MySQL, Oracle, and HSQLDB creating HIERARCHY_NODE_PARENTS
  - Added a fixupDatabase() migration that detects and migrates existing encoded-string parent data into the join table, then drops the obsolete columns; column detection uses JDBC metadata to avoid noisy SQL error logging

  Entity & Package Restructure
  - Deleted the old HierarchyPersistentNode, HierarchyNodeMetaData, HierarchyNodePermission DAO model classes and their Hibernate .hbm.xml mapping files
  - Deleted the old HierarchyNode DTO (which existed only to expose decoded Set<String> to callers)
  - Created new HierarchyNode and HierarchyNodePermission JPA entities in org.sakaiproject.hierarchy.model — the package external callers already imported, so no import changes needed outside the module

  Repository Layer
  - Replaced the old HierarchyDao / HierarchyDaoImpl / genericdao pattern with Spring-style HierarchyNodeRepository and HierarchyNodePermissionRepository interfaces backed by SpringCrudRepositoryImpl
  - Added findAllAncestors / findAllDescendants using ANSI WITH RECURSIVE CTEs (replacing manual transitive closure propagation), with HSQLDB-compatible explicit column list syntax
  - Annotated all read-only repository methods with [user](readOnly = true)

  Service (HierarchyServiceImpl)
  - Rewrote from ~1,177 lines to ~555 lines by removing all encode/decode logic, all manual transitive-closure propagation loops, and the DTO conversion layer
  - addNode / addChildRelation / removeChildRelation / removeNode operate directly on the JPA entity graph
  - Bidirectional inverse-side collections kept in sync manually (the mappedBy side is not auto-updated by Hibernate)
  - removeNode simplified: clears owning side, removes node from parent's children in memory, deletes — no redundant save, no re-lookup, no refresh
  - All read-only public methods annotated [user](readOnly = true)
  - Captured return values from all save() calls; replaced .getId().equals() with .equals() (Lombok generates equals/hashCode on id)

  Deleted Dead Code
  - HierarchyImplUtils (encode/decode utilities) — deleted entirely
  - HierarchyImplUtilsTest — deleted
  - HierarchyDaoImpl, ResourceFinder — deleted
  - Old HierarchyServiceImplTest (1,512 lines) replaced with a clean rewrite (1,394 lines)
  - Old spring-hibernate.xml, sakai-hibernate.xml, hibernate-test.xml wire-up files replaced with components.xml and a Spring Java config test class

  Delegated Access Callers
  - HierarchyNodeSerialized: updated constructor to use getters; childNodeIds/parentNodeIds (transitive closure) left as empty sets since pre-computation was removed
  - DelegatedAccessSiteHierarchyJob: replaced all direct field access with getters; in-loop child tracking updated to mutate getChildren() so getDirectChildNodeIds() stays consistent
  - ProjectLogicImpl: replaced all direct field access with getters; removeNode, siteNodes traversal, and shopping-period checks updated to call getChildNodes/getParentNodes through the service

* **New Features**
  * Bulk ancestor/descendant and direct-parent/child lookups plus expanded permission and delegated-access user lookup APIs.

title: SAK-52568 webapi Document notifications and dashboards with wired controller tests
body:
https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52568

Document the notifications and dashboard endpoints with request and response examples generated by Spring REST Docs. Correct unauthenticated response codes to `403 Forbidden`, dashboard response descriptions, login form-parameter includes, and the documentation entry point. Generated request examples include the `/api` context path.

Controller documentation tests use Spring-managed controllers, reset shared boundary mocks between tests, and configure dashboard behavior through Sakai configuration rather than private fields. Add notification authentication and messaging-failure coverage.

Add 13 MVC integration tests that load the unmodified production `WebMvcConfiguration`, its complete component scan, and `webAppContextSetup`. Exercise the real controllers, bearer interceptor, discovered exception advice, JSON converters, formatter registration, dashboard initialization, and resource handlers. Cover bearer rejection with an existing session, temporary principal use and session restoration after success and controller failure, and the `/login`, `/docs/**`, and `/webjars/**` interceptor exclusions.

Mocks are confined to named kernel and other-module boundary services; no Web API MVC components are mocked. Test-only Jakarta Mail, Spring ORM, and Hibernate dependencies supply types exposed by those boundary APIs. Production application code and runtime wiring remain unchanged from master.

Scope: the MVC integration tests do not run the servlet container's Sakai RequestFilter/listeners or verify token cryptography, backend authorization, or persistence implementations.

Validation:
- Rebased onto `upstream/master` at `e4a49d929a7`, preserving upstream login documentation and tag authorization coverage.
- `mvn -o -pl webapi clean verify -Dsurefire.runOrder=random`: all 90 tests passed; Web API WAR and HTML documentation generated successfully.
- Temporarily removing the interceptor registration, route exclusions, or formatter registration caused the corresponding integration tests to fail; production source restored afterward.
- Packaged WAR excludes test classes and fixtures; generated documentation has no missing includes or unresolved directives.
- `git diff --check` passed.

title: SAK-52576 LTI fix stealthed tool link launches
body:
SAK-50758 tightened non-admin LTI tool lookup so global stealthed tools are only visible to a site when an explicit lti_tool_site deployment row exists. That is correct after a stealthed deployment is removed, but existing LTI content links created while the tool was visible may only have lti_content.tool_id and no matching deployment row.

When an admin later changes that tool to stealth, existing Assignments, Lessons, and site navigation links still point at the content row, but callers resolve the associated tool through getTool(toolKey, siteId). Without a deployment row, that lookup returns null, so consumers treat the item as deleted or misconfigured. The visible symptom is the launch error 'External tool item is missing or improperly configured' and a '-' launch URL in the Tool Links list when the URL should be inherited from the tool.

There was a second issue in the new-link path. insertToolContentDao already had logic to auto-deploy a stealthed tool to the target site for admins, but it compared a Long visible value with the int LTI_VISIBLE_STEALTH using Long.equals(Integer). That comparison is always false, so the deployment row was never inserted for newly created stealthed links either.

Fix this by adding deployment rows for every existing site that already has lti_content rows for a tool when that tool transitions into stealth, joining SAKAI_SITE so stale or orphaned content site ids are not revived. This preserves existing links at the moment the visibility changes while preserving the SAK-50758 removal behavior: if an admin later removes a deployment row, getTool will again hide that stealthed tool from the site. Also use numeric comparison for the Long visible value so new admin-created stealthed links are deployed correctly.

title: SAK-52636 Calendar iCal export uses RRULE for recurring events
body:
Replace the long-standing TBD placeholder in generateICal() with a proper implementation. Previously, recurring events were expanded into individual VEVENT occurrences; external clients (Google Calendar, Outlook, Apple Calendar) had no way to recognise them as a series.

generateICal() now iterates each calendar individually and calls getEvents(null, null) to retrieve base events without recurrence expansion. One-time events outside the export window are filtered as before. Recurring events are always included and get an RRULE built from their RecurrenceRule.

New helper buildRRule() maps all Sakai recurrence types to standard iCal:
  Daily → FREQ=DAILY
  Weekly → FREQ=WEEKLY
  MWF → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR
  TTh → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU,TH
  MW → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE
  SMW → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU,MO,WE
  SMTW → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU,MO,TU,WE
  STT → FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU,TU,TH
  Monthly → FREQ=MONTHLY
  Yearly → FREQ=YEARLY

INTERVAL, COUNT and UNTIL are included when set on the rule.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Enhanced iCal export producing richer event entries (organizer, location, comments, attachments), with improved timezone handling.

* **Bug Fixes & Enhancements**
  * More accurate recurrence support: emits RRULEs and EXDATEs for excluded instances and sequence exclusions.
  * Better filtering of one-time vs recurring events during export and graceful skipping when calendars/events are unavailable.

title: SAK-52652 Calendar UX improvements
body:
## Summary

Several usability improvements to the FullCalendar-based Calendar tool view:

- **Click a day in Month view → Day view**: clicking a day cell navigates to the Day view for that date.
- **Double-click a time slot → New event**: in Day/Week view, double-clicking a time slot opens the "New event" form with that date and time prefilled. `CalendarAction.doNew()` now reads `newEventDate`/`newEventHour`/`newEventMinute` parameters submitted by a hidden form.

- **Fix `scrollTime` reset**: the height change above causes FullCalendar to remount the time grid's scroll container on next render, which was resetting the configured `scrollTime` back to its default. Now reapplied after the remount.

title: SAK-52477 Search align bouncycastle version
body:
Search was explicitly declaring bcprov-jdk15on:1.70 and bcmail-jdk15on:1.70. Those are from the old Bouncy Castle jdk15on artifact line. Current Search already gets the modern jdk18on Bouncy Castle artifacts through Tika 3.3.1, specifically 1.84. Keeping
  the old explicit jars meant Search could carry both old jdk15on and modern jdk18on Bouncy Castle families on the classpath, which is exactly the kind of duplicate crypto-provider setup that can cause version/linkage ambiguity at runtime.

  The original PR from [user]  removed the obsolete Search declarations. After rebasing it onto current upstream/master, we found one remaining item: Kernel directly declared `bcprov-jdk18on:1.83`, while the current Tika brings BouncyCastle `jdk18on:1.84`. Our
  commit updates Kernel’s direct bcprov-jdk18on dependency from 1.83 to 1.84, so Kernel and Search now resolve the same Bouncy Castle line.

title: SAK-52598 DateManager add term-rollover date tools (per-column fill, Smart Shift, Bulk Anchor)
body:
> **Title note:** once I have a Jira key this should become
> `SAK-##### DateManager add term-rollover date tools (per-column fill, Smart Shift, Bulk Anchor)`
> to match the `<issue key> <component> <brief description>` convention. See the Jira note at the bottom.

## Summary

Follow-up to #14504 (SAK-52523, *DateManager add bulk date setter controls*). That PR added a global bulk
setter; this one builds on it to make **rolling a copied course into a new term** fast and intuitive. When a
site is copied from a previous term, an instructor needs an easy way to re-set every date for the new academic
calendar — this adds three complementary tools plus a layout that keeps them out of the way of per-item editing.

## What's new

- **Per-column bulk fill** — each editable date column header gets a small date box + a ↓ button that fills
  every row of that one column, in that one section, with the entered date.
- **Bulk Anchor** — a term-date matrix (Classes Start, Classes End, Exam Begins, Exam Ends) with a checkbox
  per column across every tool, so one named date can be mapped onto whichever columns you tick. Overlapping
  ticks apply top-to-bottom (lower row wins).
- **Smart Shift** — re-anchors *all* dated items between a new **first** and **last** date: the earliest date
  lands on the new first, the latest on the new last, and everything in between is spread proportionally. With
  **Snap to weeks** on, each item keeps its own weekday and time-of-day and moves only by whole weeks, so the
  weekly cadence of a copied course survives a move into a shorter/longer term. (Distinct from the existing
  offset shifter, which keeps spacing exact but lets the end float.)
- **Fill-mode toggle** — apply to *every* cell (empty + existing) or *only cells that already have a date*.
- **Layout** — the batch tools are grouped behind a coloured accent bar under a "Bulk editing tools" heading,
  each in a collapsible card (the raw offset shifter expanded by default), and separated by a rule from the
  per-tool "Edit individual items" sections, so the editing grid is what you see on load.

## Bug fix included

`localDatePicker` writes its hidden field as ISO8601 **with a timezone offset** (e.g.
`2026-09-01T09:00:00+02:00`), but the apply paths parsed it with offset-less strict formats, so every apply
silently no-op'd. Added `DTMN.parseInputDateValue` which strips the trailing offset (and the time for date-only
gradebook fields) before parsing in the user's Sakai timezone. All date math goes through
`moment.tz(..., userTimeZone)` with a guarded fallback.

## Tests

- **Automated:** a standalone `node --test` unit suite under `tool/src/test/js/` (20 tests) covering the pure
  date logic — `parseInputDateValue` (regression guard for the offset bug), `snapToSourceWeekday`,
  `computeFittedDate` (the Smart Shift math, extracted from `fitDates` for testability), format round-trips, and
  timezone handling. It loads the shipped `initDatePicker.js` into a Node `vm` context with the real
  `moment-timezone`, so it exercises the actual code. **It is intentionally not wired into the Maven build** (the
  WAR packages `src/main/webapp` only) — happy to wire it into CI via `frontend-maven-plugin` if you'd like.
  Run with `cd site-manage/datemanager/tool/src/test/js && npm install && npm test`.
- **Manual:** I manually tested this end-to-end on a local Sakai test site — per-column fill (all vs
  existing-only), Smart Shift (multi-item spread + weekly snap), Bulk Anchor matrix, gradebook date-only
  handling, and the save/confirm flow.

## Compliance with the prior review (#14504)

I went back through the CodeRabbit findings on #14504 since this touches the same files, and confirmed:
timezone math runs in the Sakai user zone (not the browser), `getUserTimeZone()` is guarded with optional
chaining, the apply path uses the proper formatter and syncs the hidden field, gradebook columns are treated as
date-only, inputs are self-closing, and the new element IDs are kebab-case.

Apereo CLA, and as I mentioned I'd like to do this properly for future contributions: **could I be invited to

body:
https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52696

## What this does

Adds server-side search and several new **View** filters to the Announcements list, so instructors can quickly find announcements in busy sites instead of scrolling the full list.

### View filters (new options in the View dropdown)
- **Published** — posted, past their release date, and not retracted
- **Scheduled** — not a draft, but with a release date still in the future
- **Drafts** — hidden/draft messages the user is permitted to see
- **My Announcements** — messages authored by the current user

The Published / Scheduled / Drafts / My Announcements options are gated on `$allow_new`, so they only appear for users who can author announcements.

### Search
- Reuses the shared `#searchFilterPanel` macro to add a search box above the View dropdown, wired to the base `doSearch` / `doSearch_clear` actions.
- Filtering happens server-side in `filterMessagesBySearch(...)`, matching the term case-insensitively against **subject, author display name, and body**.
- Filtering is applied to the full viewable list *before* paging/trimming, so the result counts and pager stay authoritative across all pages.
- Matched terms are highlighted with `<mark>` in the subject column (`announcements.js`), re-running after the shared macro swaps in fresh rows via the `sfp:updated` event. Highlighting is presentation-only — the server has already scoped the rows. The regex input is escaped and the 3-char minimum mirrors `MIN_SEARCH_CHARS` in the shared macro.

## Implementation notes
- New `getMessagesDrafts / getMessagesPosted / getMessagesScheduled / getMessagesMine` each start from `getMessages(...)`, which already applies the tool's permission and viewability checks, then narrow the list — so no new permission surface is introduced. Drafts still rely on the existing author / `annc.read.drafts` gating.
- `isScheduled(...)` reads `AnnouncementService.RELEASE_DATE` and returns false when no release date is set.
- Fixed a pre-existing typo in the `view.all` option (`"'view.all"` → `"view.all"`) so the "All" option renders selected correctly.
- Assignments: added an `id="assignments-list"` to the assignments list table (and `id="announcements-list"` to the announcements table) so the shared search macro can target the table body. No behavior change in Assignments.

## SAK-52697 Site Info → Add Participants: accept delimited / smart email lists https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52697 ### What Currently the **Add Participants** helper requires one entry per line. This PR lets instructors paste account lists in the formats they actually have on hand (comma / semicolon / whitespace separated, or messy blobs that mix emails with names and punctuation) without hand-reformatting them first. ### Changes - **Input format per box** — each account textarea gains a format: `smart` (default), `delimited`, or `line`. - `smart` — auto-detects at the blob level: if the paste contains an `@`, every email-format token is extracted (surrounding names/punctuation/delimiters ignored); otherwise it's treated as a username list split on any delimiter. - `delimited` — any run of comma / semicolon / whitespace collapses to one entry per line. - `line` — unchanged legacy behaviour, preserving the non-official `email,lastName,firstName` per-line format. - **Explicit Account type radio** (`auto` / `email` / `username`) for the official box. Because smart extraction relies on an email regex that can't match bare usernames, choosing *username* falls back to plain delimited splitting (`effectiveOfficialMode`). - **Per-entry lookup routing** — emails vs usernames (eids) are resolved appropriately; `EMAIL_EXTRACT_PATTERN` drives both the smart extraction and the auto-detection. - **Live parsed-count** — a small note under each box shows how many entries were parsed from the paste, mirroring the server-side normalization so users get immediate feedback. Kept in an external JS file (`parsed-count.js`) because the RSF/IKAT template is processed as XML and mangles inline scripts; the script anchors off static count `

title: SAK-52706 Portal: dynamic variables in rich text content with an editor Variables dropdown
body:
https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52706

Instructors hard-code term-specific values (term name, first/final day of classes, instructor contact) into rich text content, and every term rollover they go stale. This adds **dynamic variables**: `{{token}}` placeholders that work anywhere the rich text editor is used and render as live values at display time.

## How it works

- When `portal.termtokens.enabled=true` (**default false**), `SkinnableCharonPortal` injects a `sakai.termsInfo` data object plus `/library/js/sakai-term-tokens.js` into every tool page head — the same pattern MathJax uses (also mirrored in `EditorServlet` per the comment there).
- Term data comes from CourseManagement (`AcademicSession` via the site's `term_eid` property) through a new `PortalService.getTermTokensScript(Site)`, formatted server-side in the viewer's locale/timezone via `UserTimeService`. Site/term data is cached ~10 min per site/term/locale/timezone/day; the reader's own fields (name/email) are computed per request and never cached.
- The display script substitutes an **exact allowlist** of tokens in rendered text nodes (TreeWalker + MutationObserver for ajax/lit content) and skips `script/style/textarea/contenteditable/.cke` subtrees, so authors always see raw tokens while editing and arbitrary `{{...}}` (mustache templates etc.) is never touched. Stored content keeps the raw tokens — nothing is rewritten at save time, so real-time values like current term keep updating forever.
- "Current term" is date-aware (a session whose range covers today, preferring admin-flagged current sessions) so it rolls over automatically rather than relying solely on the `IS_CURRENT` flag.

## Authoring UX

A new CKEditor richcombo dropdown (**Variables**, between Templates and Source in the full toolbar) lists every available variable by friendly name with a live preview of its value and an explanatory hover tooltip, grouped into categories: *This Course*, *Term Dates*, *Right Now*, *The Reader*. Variables without data for the site (e.g. project sites with no term) simply don't appear.

29 variables: course title, term name/code/year, first & final day of term (long + short), week of term / weeks in term / days left in term, current term (name/code/dates), next term (+ first day), instructor name/email (site contact), institution name, site link, today's date / day of week / month / year, and the reader's own first/last/full name and email (consistent with the Lessons `lessonbuilder.personalize.text` tokens, which this generalizes).

The dropdown panel is themed with the Sakai design tokens (including dark mode — CKEditor panels are iframes, so the plugin mirrors the theme class onto the panel document the same way SAK-44562 does for the editing area, and the default skin now themes `.cke_panel`).

## Also fixed

`CKEDITOR.timestamp` was never set, so browsers cached Sakai's custom editor plugins/lang files indefinitely (even across Sakai upgrades). It is now keyed to the portal CDN version so editor resources cache-bust like the rest of the portal's static assets.

## Testing

- 6 new unit tests (`PortalServiceTermTokensTests`, module suite 16→17 green): disabled flag, null site, full field emission incl. ISO dates and week math, EcmaScript escaping of hostile term titles, unknown-term fallback, date-aware current-term selection.
- Verified end-to-end in a dockerized instance: Lessons text items, Overview / Site Information Display, project sites (no term), locale date formatting, kill switch off ⇒ raw tokens and no dropdown, decoy tokens preserved, MathJax coexistence.

## Known v1 limitations

Substitution happens in the DOM, so email notifications / RSS / search index see raw tokens — a server-side helper for those paths is a natural follow-up, as is per-site custom dates (add/drop deadline, finals week) which core Sakai has no data model for.

title: SAK-34476 Samigo: block feedback dates that reveal answers after submission
body:
https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-34476

## Problem

With Feedback Delivery set to "displayed to the student at a specific date", Samigo never checks that the feedback date falls after the assessment's final submission deadline. If the feedback date is in the past while the assessment is still open — the classic case is duplicating or importing last term's assessment and updating the due date but forgetting the feedback date — every student taking it after that date gets a "Show Feedback" link mid-take that reveals correct answers and per-question scores (the Table of Contents shows running scores too). Two instructors at UVA hit exactly this and reported it as a bug; the T&L and UX calls agreed the fix is to prevent the configuration at save time (see ticket comments for the agreed spec).

## Fix

New `FeedbackDateValidator` computes the **latest submission deadline** — due date, or the late acceptance date when late submissions are enabled, pushed out by the due/retract date of every extended-time exception — and blocks saving/publishing when the feedback date falls before it (or when no deadline exists at all), per the spec in the ticket. When any cohort (base students or an exception holder) is open-ended, there is no safe feedback date, so the save is blocked with a message asking for a deadline; this matches delivery behavior, where a null exception date means "no cutoff" rather than "fall back to the base date".

The check runs on **every path that can produce the bad state**, several of which skip the settings-form validations entirely today:

- draft Settings → **Save** (also closes the ticket's Publish-Confirmation → Edit Settings → Save loophole)
- draft Settings → **Save Settings and Publish**
- assessment list → Actions → **Publish** (runs `ConfirmPublishAssessmentListener` with `isFromAssessmentSettings=false`, which previously skipped all date checks)
- assessment list → checkboxes → **Publish Selected** (went straight to `publishOne()` with no validation; blocked per assessment, named in the message)
- published assessment Settings → **Save**

The error messages tell the instructor the deadline (formatted with `UserTimeService` in the site/user locale) and point to the "Yes, show the student feedback while they are taking the assessment" option for anyone who wants mid-take feedback on purpose. On rejection the Grading and Feedback settings panel is auto-expanded so the instructor lands on the field to fix.

**Retract is deliberately exempted** (`!retractNow`): retracting closes the assessment and ends any leak, so it must never be blocked by this check — otherwise an instructor couldn't shut down a leaking assessment.

## Known limitations (intentional — scoped to the authoring paths this ticket describes)

- **Republish of a retracted-for-edit assessment is left alone.** `ConfirmRepublishAssessmentListener` only re-checks scores (its date-check call has been commented out for years). An assessment republished without editing keeps dates that were validated on their last save, so the residual exposure is limited to data saved before this fix — consistent with not retroactively validating existing published data. Flagging rather than expanding scope; happy to follow up if reviewers prefer it guarded too.
- **Existing published assessments** with a stale feedback date keep their current behavior until an instructor next edits their settings; there is no delivery-time enforcement (per the ticket discussion, silently overriding instructor settings at delivery was rejected). The delivery-side weakness that makes the mid-take reveal possible at all — the take screen trusts a `showfeedbacknow` request parameter — is SAK-52707 and is best fixed there.
- **Date Manager** edits Samigo dates through its own service (`DateManagerServiceImpl.updateAssessments`, plus its CSV import) and performs no feedback-vs-deadline check, so it can still move a published assessment into the bad state — tracked separately in SAK-43763.
- **`PATCH /api/sites/{siteId}/entities`** (webapi `SiteEntityController`) can likewise move a published assessment's due date or rewrite its extended-time exceptions past an existing feedback date with no validation.
- **Lessons Common Cartridge import** is the one caller of `publishAssessment` outside the publish listener; it blanks the access control on import, so dates are normally null, but it does bypass this validation.
- **Exception holders on a "no late submissions" assessment**: delivery treats an extended-time student whose entry has no retract date as accept-late indefinitely (`DeliveryBean.isAcceptLateSubmission`), so such a student who never submitted can still begin after the feedback date. Guarding that here would block feedback-by-date on every no-late assessment with exceptions, so it is left to the delivery-side fix (SAK-52707).

## Testing

- New `FeedbackDateValidatorTest` (15 tests) covers the deadline computation: base due/retract with and without late handling, null deadlines, exceptions extending (but never shrinking) the deadline, open-ended cohorts poisoning the deadline, and the feedback-date comparison boundaries (equal-to-deadline allowed).
- Manually verified on a local instance: each path above blocks with the message when the feedback date is stale and proceeds normally once the date is corrected (or a different feedback option is selected); Retract still works on an assessment with a stale feedback date.

title: SAK-52707 Samigo: never reveal by-date feedback during an active take
body:
https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52707

> **Draft / first pass for discussion.** This is a focused delivery-side change and I'm opening it to get eyes on the approach before polishing. I'm not certain it fully fits Sakai's security model or that gating purely on Immediate Feedback won't have side effects on flows I haven't exercised — see "Open questions" below. Feedback very welcome on whether this is the right layer to enforce at.

## Problem

While a student is actively taking an assessment, whether feedback (correct answers, question-level feedback) is shown is decided from client-supplied input with no server-side entitlement check:

- `DeliveryActionListener.setFeedbackMode(...)` sets `delivery.feedback = "true"` for take / take-via-url actions whenever the request carries `showfeedbacknow=true`, with no check that feedback is actually available. The item JSPs then render correct answers and question-level feedback off `delivery.feedback` alone.
- `DeliveryBean.getShowFeedbackLink()` rendered the mid-take Feedback link when `getShowImmediate() || feedbackOnDate`. `feedbackOnDate` is true whenever feedback delivery is "on specific dates" and that date has passed — so the hidden link was the only thing enforcing policy.

Result: a crafted request can reveal feedback mid-take even on a correctly configured "on specific dates" assessment, and through the normal UI on a post-deadline retake/resubmit once the feedback date has passed. This is the delivery-side companion to SAK-34476 (authoring-side date validation, #14735), which prevents the *misconfiguration* but does not close this gap on a properly configured assessment.

## Approach in this pass

"On specific dates" feedback is intended for review after submission; only Immediate Feedback is meant to display feedback during a take. So during an active take, gate on Immediate Feedback in both places:

- `getShowFeedbackLink()` — for take / take-via-url, return the link only when `getShowImmediate()`; `feedbackOnDate` no longer surfaces it mid-take. Preview and review are unchanged (they still honor `feedbackOnDate`).
- `setFeedbackMode()` — for take / take-via-url, honor `showfeedbacknow=true` only when `getShowImmediate()` is also true, so a forged parameter is ignored. Preview (case 2), review (case 3), and grade (case 4) are untouched.

Two files, no new bundle strings or schema changes.

## What this deliberately does *not* do

- No delivery-time enforcement of the *authoring* rule (feedback date vs. submission deadline) — that stays on the authoring side in SAK-34476/#14735, per the ticket discussion that rejected silently overriding instructor settings at delivery.
- Does not touch how feedback is shown in review/history after submission.

## Open questions for reviewers

- **Is delivery the right layer, and is "Immediate Feedback only during a take" the correct policy?** It matches the ticket's stated intent, but I'd like confirmation it doesn't contradict an intended use of by-date feedback mid-take that I'm not aware of.
- **Preview parity.** Preview (instructor) still trusts `showfeedbacknow` unconditionally (case 2). That seems right since preview is instructor-only, but flagging it explicitly.
- **Post-deadline retake behavior change.** A legitimate post-deadline retake of a by-date assessment no longer shows the Feedback link mid-retake. I believe that's the intended fix, but it is a user-visible behavior change worth a second opinion.
- **Coverage of take entry points.** I've matched action modes 1 (take) and 5 (take-via-url) and the two take action strings; if there are other delivery entry points that should count as "taking," they need the same gate.

## Testing so far

- Manual forge check against a running instance: on an assessment whose feedback date is correctly in the future, a `showfeedbacknow=true` POST during a take previously returned item feedback including correct-answer text; with this change it does not.
- Not yet added automated coverage — `setFeedbackMode` / `getShowFeedbackLink` have no existing unit harness and need JSF/bean wiring; happy to add tests if the approach is agreed.
